title: Arkret SealTransparency
description: Seal transparency wire objects (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.4): an append-only log entry binding one accepted Seal tuple, and an independent auditor attestation over a log range. The log makes split-view attacks (showing different Seal chains to different receivers) detectable: an operator must either publish consistently or fork the log, and a log fork is provable from two signed entries with the same log_index. Top-level object is a log entry; auditor attestations use #/$defs/auditor_attestation.

log_id.description: Stable identifier of the transparency log (operator URL, DID, or registry name).

log_index.description: Zero-based append-only position. Two differently-signed entries with the same (log_id, log_index) are a provable log fork.

prev_entry_digest.description: Digest of the previous entry's canonical bytes (hash chain). null only for log_index 0.

auditor_attestation.description: Signed statement by an independent auditor (peer Realm or third party) that it verified the log range [from_index, to_index]: append-only consistency, Seal signature validity, and control/completeness monotonicity along every Seal DAG predecessor edge represented in the range. Log-index-adjacent concurrent leaves are not compared. A client accepts this as verified v1 evidence only when a concrete operation/profile carries it and the deployment policy's required attestation count is met.

head_entry_digest.description: Digest of the entry at to_index, binding the attested range head.

checks.description: All checks MUST be true. dag_edges_verified means monotonic checks were performed along every represented predecessor edge, not by log_index adjacency; an auditor that cannot assert a check MUST NOT issue the attestation.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical entry / attestation bytes with the signature field omitted.
